I take that seriously enough not to add. What answers it for holding is the distinction between the front end and the long end: a hike raises the 2Y mechanically, but it lowers the long end's expected terminal path if it works, and the 2s10s at +0.28 is flat enough that the long end is no longer pricing an inflation spiral. The higher-low sequence and the reclaimed 50dma are the market beginning to agree, and yesterday's green close against a 2% equity drawdown is the behaviour of a hedge, not of a casualty.

key_risk: The risk of closing is that DKS beats and gaps up, and a 44%-off-the-high retailer with a 4.87% ATR can add 10% on a good print just as easily as it can lose it - that is the symmetric cost of flattening before a binary event. I am accepting that cost deliberately rather than claiming the print will be bad; I have no edge on the direction of the reaction, which is precisely the point. The expectancy figure above will fail `check_expectancy` in validation. That flag is correct and is the justification for the close, not an error to be tuned away - if this candidate is demoted to the watchlist, the close instruction still stands.

That case is real and I cannot refute it on the fundamentals. What decides it is that it is an argument for a *new* position sized for an event, with a stop set wide enough to survive a gap, and not an argument for keeping a position that was opened six days ago on a different thesis with a stop that this event will skip over. If the reaction is good, the trade can be re-entered on Tuesday with levels drawn from the actual gap.

thesis: An exit on an existing long, and the decision is already made by the tape rather than by me. ONON closed 2026-11-19 at 30.82 with a session low of 30.705 - one and a half cents above the 30.69 stop, or 0.07 ATR on an instrument whose ATR(14) is 1.81, a full 5.88% of price. Closing at the open converts an almost-certain stop-out at an unknown gap price into a known one. The trend behind it is unambiguous: 38.62 on 2026-11-04 down to 30.82 in eleven sessions, now 25.6% off the 150-day high of 41.41, below both the 20dma of 34.17 and the 50dma of 32.54.
key_risk: The risk of closing a hair above the stop is the worst outcome in trading - exiting at the exact low and watching it reverse, which on a 5.88% ATR name can be a 10% bounce within two sessions. Accepting that is the cost of not letting an opening gap pick the exit price. The published expectancy is well below the 2.05:1 break-even baseline of 33%, which will fail `check_expectancy`; that flag is the justification for the close rather than an error, and if this is demoted to the watchlist the instruction to close still stands.
counter_argument: The case for holding is that the stop is 1.5 cents away, so holding costs almost nothing versus closing - if the stop is hit you lose the same amount you would by selling, and if it is not you keep the upside for free. That is nearly right, and it is the only reason this is a conviction-3 call rather than a 4. What breaks it is gap risk in the direction the tape is actually moving: the market closed at its session low across every index fetched, so the probability-weighted opening price is below 30.705, not at it. A stop order in that session does not fill at 30.69, it fills wherever the gap lands - and the free optionality only exists if the stop fills at the stop.

thesis: This is a correction of a call I nearly made in this run's own notes, and the correction matters more than the idea. At 06:40 I flagged LEN for cancellation on the grounds that a homebuilder is the worst-positioned long in a Fed hiking cycle with the 10Y at 5.07%. That reasoning overrides a valuation thesis with a macro view, and it is backwards: a sub-book price in a quality builder is produced BY the rate cycle, so high rates are the mechanism of the discount rather than a refutation of it. The thesis is unchanged from 2026-11-13 - accumulate below roughly 0.9x book toward a 1.20x book target of 108.50, in the same 77.12-81.90 band Berkshire bought on 2026-10-02 - and `config/strategy.md` is explicit that a long-term idea legitimately repeats while accumulation is unfinished. The accumulation plan was already built to absorb this: thirds at 84.00, 81.00 and 77.50, with a fourth under 72.00.
key_risk: The invalidation is a development, not a price, because there is no stop on this position. The thesis is wrong if reported book value per share stops compounding - specifically two consecutive quarters of declining equity per share, or inventory impairments large enough to mark the land book down - because the entire case is paying under book for an asset base that grows. A second invalidation is a deliberate strategy shift into land-light joint ventures at materially worse returns on equity. Falling order volumes and falling margins are expected in this rate environment and are already the reason for the entry price; they are not the invalidation.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that homebuilder book value is not a floor the way financial book value is - land and work-in-progress inventory is carried at cost, and in a genuine housing downturn it gets impaired, so 0.9x book can become 1.3x a written-down book without the price moving. That is the real risk and it is what the 68.00 bear case is meant to price, being roughly the 2026 low area and a 15% markdown on the equity. What answers it for now is that the rate shock is a demand-side event with the labour market still at 4.1% unemployment, which is the configuration where builders cut price and pace rather than impair, and that Berkshire underwrote the same land book at these prices seven weeks ago.

evidence.detail: Target 108.50 is 1.20x stated book value per share, against an entry near 79.50 that is roughly 0.9x - the method is the multiple of reported equity per share, reassessed quarterly as book compounds, not a chart level. The 68.00 bear case is a ~15% markdown of that equity.

Berkshire Hathaway bought LEN in the 77.12-81.90 band on 2026-10-02 - the same band this accumulation plan uses - which is an independent underwriter of the land book at this price rather than a view on the chart.

thesis: This is an order-hygiene recommendation and the third time it has been made, which is itself the finding. The 406.77 gold short has been resting unfilled since 2026-09-08 while GLD fell to 335.18 - a 17.6% decline, straight through the 355.00 target - and it is still showing as live in today's prior context. The idea was directionally right and earned nothing, because the entry sat above the market and required a rally first. Worse, it is now a latent risk rather than a dead letter: a stale limit 21% above spot is an order to short gold into a violent squeeze, which is the one circumstance where this position would be badly wrong. Cancel it.
key_risk: The risk of cancelling is nil - there is no position and no exposure is being given up. The risk of NOT cancelling is a fill on a gold spike, in a tape where a hiking Fed is the reason gold fell 1.76% on 2026-11-19, and any reversal of that rate expectation would move gold up fast and fill this order at the worst possible moment. Conviction is 3 rather than higher only because the evidence is two kinds and this is bookkeeping, not an edge.
counter_argument: The case for leaving it is that an unfilled limit costs nothing to carry and preserves optionality if gold does rally back to 406.77, where the short thesis would be valid again. That is wrong on its own terms: at 406.77 the original thesis - gold extended and rolling over - would have been refuted by a 21% advance, so the order would be filling precisely because its premise had failed. A limit order is not a free option when the price that triggers it is the price that invalidates it.

evidence.detail: GLD closed 335.18 on 2026-11-19 (open 339.88, high 340.52, low 335.05), down 1.76%. The 406.77 entry is 21.4% above that close and the 355.00 target is 19.94 above spot - the target was passed without a fill.

The free-optionality argument fails because the trigger price and the invalidation price are the same number: a fill at 406.77 requires a 21% rally that would itself refute the roll-over premise. Supported by the mechanism now driving gold - it fell with equities on 2026-11-19 on rising real rates, so the rally that fills this order is a rate reversal, the state in which short gold loses most.

thesis: The second of two stale short orders, and together they are the lesson rather than two separate misses. This 74,075 micro-bitcoin short was published 2026-11-09 and required BTC to rally into it before paying; instead BTC fell 16.4% to 61,921, straight through the 63,500 first target and to within 2,921 of the 59,000 second. The thesis was right, the direction was right, the position never existed. Paired with the GLD short - also right, also unfilled, also 21% away - this is a systematic entry-placement failure, not luck: both orders were set on the wrong side of the market, so the only tape that filled them was the one that refuted them. Cancel it, and note that /MBTZ6 is now a near-expiry December contract besides.
key_risk: Nothing is risked by cancelling, since no position exists. The live risk is the order itself: leaving a market-order short resting 19.6% above spot means initiating leveraged short bitcoin exposure into a 20% rally, and a futures stop is a margin event rather than an exit. `config/universe.md` also requires naming the contract month and flagging a contract near its final trading week - /MBTZ6 is the December contract, so it would need rolling almost immediately even if the thesis were still live.
counter_argument: The case against cancelling is that bitcoin at 61,921 in a Fed hiking cycle is still a short, so why remove the exposure - just re-enter lower. That conflates two decisions. Cancelling a dead order is unambiguous and costs nothing; initiating a NEW short after a 16.4% decline is a separate trade that has to clear the floors on its own, and it does not. The 2.5 ATR swing floor for futures measured off a 61,921 spot requires a stop materially above the entry while the first target has already been reached, which leaves no reward-to-risk worth 2.0. Right about direction is not the same as a trade being available, and chasing is how it becomes a loss.

evidence.detail: BTC spot 61,921 on 2026-11-20 06:01 ET, -2.81% over 24h, against a 74,075 entry (19.6% above) and a 63,500 published first target already exceeded by 1,579. ETH 1,753.48 (-2.68%) and SOL 72.28 (-2.89%) confirm the move was the whole asset class, not one coin.

The re-enter-lower argument is answered with the floors rather than dismissed: config/strategy.md sets a 2.5 ATR stop floor for futures swing and a 2.0 reward-to-risk floor, and with the first target already passed below spot there is no entry/target pair at 61,921 that clears both. The order being cancelled and a new short being declined are two separate conclusions and both hold.

thesis: This is an existing short, not a new idea, and the update is that the setup confirmed. IWM closed 2026-11-19 at 264.22, a new 150-day low, completing a clean sequence of lower lows - 270.52 (Nov 5), 267.87 (Nov 17), 263.74 (Nov 19) - while closing 0.48 off the session low on 31.4M shares against a ~22M recent average. The mechanism is rates: with the 10Y at 5.07% and the 2Y at 4.80%, floating-rate and near-dated refinancing cost is repricing against the most levered, least-profitable cohort in the US market, and the Russell carries both. The near catalyst is dated rather than vague: October core PCE prints 2026-11-25 at 08:30 ET and is the last major inflation reading before the December 9 FOMC, because November CPI does not arrive until December 10 - the day after the decision. With a 25bp December hike already 91-92c on Kalshi, that print's real work is on the undecided January meeting, quoted 59-61c hike against 39-40c hold.
key_risk: Small caps are the highest-beta thing in the market to a dovish surprise. Any sign the Fed cuts, or a sharp drop in the long end, produces a violent short squeeze from a 13% drawdown - this is the single most crowded direction to be leaning. The stop at 284.50 is 7.7% above spot, which is wide on purpose (2.4 ATR from entry) but means a full stop-out costs the whole 14-point risk. The 2026-11-25 08:30 ET core PCE print is the specific scheduled way this goes wrong, and it lands in a pre-Thanksgiving session thin enough to exaggerate the gap.
counter_argument: IWM is already 13.4% off its 120-day high and sitting on its lowest close of the period, so the obvious objection is that this is shorting into an oversold hole where the risk/reward has already been taken. That is the real risk and the reason the target is a 150-day-low extension rather than something more ambitious. What answers it is the shape of the rate curve: the 2Y at 4.80% sits 92bp ABOVE the 3.88% effective funds rate, so the market is pricing the next policy move as a tightening, not the cut that a small-cap bounce needs. Oversold is not a catalyst; a policy turn would be, and the curve says it is not coming.

evidence.detail: Closed 264.22 on 2026-11-19, a new 150-day low. Lower-low sequence from fetched daily bars: 270.52 (Nov 5) to 267.87 (Nov 17) to 263.74 (Nov 19). 20dma 277.18 and 50dma 278.91 both above price and both declining. ATR(14) 5.91.

The 2026-11-19 bar is a failed gap-up: open 271.08, high 271.80, close 264.22 within 0.48 of the 263.74 low, on 31.4M shares vs a ~22M recent average. Breadth confirms it was de-grossing rather than rotation - SPY -1.96%, QQQ -2.19%, SMH -2.62%, and GLD -1.76%, XLP -1.45%, XLU -1.24% all fell too. Only TLT closed green (+0.16%).

The oversold-bounce objection is answered with the curve, not an assertion: FRED 2026-11-18 has US2Y 4.80% against a 3.88% effective fed funds rate, a 92bp inversion of expectations that prices tightening rather than the easing a small-cap rally requires. US10Y 5.07%, 2s10s +0.28.
